topics.label: Lecture opening and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and frames the core question of what causes cancer.

topics.label: Genetic nature of cancer and sources of mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as a micro-evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous errors, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risk and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore everyday environmental exposures, the debate surrounding intrinsic versus extrinsic cancer risk, and geographical patterns in cancer epidemiology.

topics.label: Role of infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms by which pathogens and oncogenic viruses drive cancer, focusing on the cooperative etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical compounds produce DNA adducts, reactive oxygen species, and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and the two-stage model of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate cancer initiators from promoters, explaining how chronic inflammation and signaling agonists drive the proliferation of mutated cells.

topics.label: Host developmental timing and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue developmental stages influence carcinogen susceptibility and summarize the diverse pathways leading to malignancy.

topics.label: Methods for evaluating carcinogenicity and mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey genomic mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo toxicology, and in vitro assays used to evaluate carcinogens.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion: risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure in terms of everyday risk-benefit decisions and summarising key takeaways.
